simple.meaning: תָּנָה (tânâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to present (a mercenary inducement), i.e. bargain with (a harlot).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Hosea, beginning at Hosea 8:9. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תָּנָה (H8566) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: תָּנָה (tânâh) / H8566 is traced through Hosea 8:9, Hosea 8:10 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H8566. tanah I. [ תָּנָה ] verb hire (si vera lectio, akin to נתן ); — Qal Imperfect 3masculine plural בַגּוֺיִם יִתְּנוּ Hosea 8:10 hire (allies) among the nations; Hiph`il Perfect 3plural הִתְנוּ Hosea 8:9 have hired lovers. — We in both יִתְּנוּ give: 8:9 give amorous favours, 8:10 give (these), compare Now Marti Harper. — תְּנָה Psa 8:2 see נתן Qal 2 b.
